samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim second copy of `readOnlyDocStore` (an access-control boundary), and the two already differ
samples.evidence: `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts` reproduces `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` almost line for line: the same reader-allowlist rationale, the same memoized `members` map, the same `batch(fn)` special case, and the identical trap set (`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf: null`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys`) including the same non-configurable-own-property invariant carve-out in `get`. The repo's stated home for cross-engine shared logic is `@wafflebase/core` (`docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md` §Proposed package layout: pure-logic modules with subpath exports); the proxy machinery here is pure logic and parameterisable by (readers set, per-member overrides). Nothing was extracted, and the copies have already diverged: the notes version adds a `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` WeakSet for idempotence and a `HISTORY_METHODS` branch, neither of which exists in the docs version — so the same 'viewer cannot reach a write' guarantee is now implemented twice with different hardening, and a future trap fix applied to one will silently leave the other weaker.

samples.summary: Unrelated CI-flake work bundled into a sharing/auth-webhook change (scope creep)
samples.evidence: The branch's stated subjects are the notes share-link toolbar (#1044) and Yorkie auth enforce-by-default, yet it also carries a DuckDB extension warm-up plus a new `SETUP_TIMEOUT_MS` budget in `test/lakehouse-parity.e2e-spec.ts` (lakehouse connector parity — no relation to sharing, notes, or the webhook), and editor-disposal teardown fixes in `packages/docs/test/view/large-paste-indicator.test.ts` and `update-style-to-match.test.ts`. Both are defensible fixes, but they are orthogonal to the issue and to every design doc updated here, enlarging the review surface of a change that touches an access-control default.

samples.summary: New cross-cutting read-only rule table misdescribes the PDF root-seed gate, and the PDF gate diverges from the established `*InitialRootForRole` pattern
samples.evidence: `sharing.md`'s new table says root seeding is gated by "`shared-document.tsx`'s per-role `*InitialRootForRole` helpers". The PDF gate this change adds is not one of those: it is an inline `initialRoot={readOnly ? {} : initialPdfRoot()}` in `packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:212`, while the four existing types use tested helpers in `packages/frontend/src/types/*-document.ts` (`docsInitialRootForRole`, `notesInitialRootForRole`, `boardInitialRootForRole`, `sheetsInitialRootForRole`, each with a sibling unit test). So the canonical document now under-describes the very rule it exists to record, and the fifth provider is the one type whose seed gate is not expressible/testable as a pure helper like its siblings.

samples.summary: New operator-facing env vars `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET` / `TARGET_JWT_SECRET` are documented only inside the script's usage string
samples.evidence: The copy script now requires two new secrets to attach against an enforcing deployment, but a grep for `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET`/`TARGET_JWT_SECRET` finds them only in `packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts` (and a review artifact). `docs/design/document-copy.md` — which documents this script by name — `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md` (which discusses the script sending a token to a foreign deployment), `packages/backend/README.md` and `packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md` list no such variables, so an operator following the docs after enforce-by-default gets a silently anonymous, denied attach.

samples.summary: Read-path `migrateDocument` now rewrites `meta.themeId`/`masterId` for every mount, recorded only in the read-only sections of `slides-mobile.md`
samples.evidence: The new reconciliation block in `migrateDocument` changes the behaviour of the shared slides read path (editor mounts included: a deck whose `meta` pins a removed theme now renders from the first themed entry instead of throwing in `getActiveTheme`). The canonical slides doc `docs/design/slides/slides.md` describes `migrateDocument`'s read-path responsibilities (e.g. `recentColors` copy-through at line 529) but is not updated; the change is explained only in `slides-mobile.md`/`notes` read-only prose, i.e. filed under the feature that discovered it rather than the subsystem doc that owns the migration.

samples.summary: `sideTokenInjector` reimplements `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv`'s read-env-warn-or-inject shape instead of parameterising it
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv(secret = process.env.JWT_SECRET, …)` already does 'read a secret from the environment, warn and return `undefined` when missing, otherwise return an injector'. `sideTokenInjector` duplicates that control flow with a per-side message; passing the env var name (or just `process.env[envVar]`) into the shared helper would have kept one warn/return contract.

verdict.reason: The duplication is present as described. notes/src/store/read-only.ts:93-195 reproduces docs/src/store/read-only.ts:67-169 near line-for-line: same reader-allowlist rationale (notes:3-18 vs docs:3-20; notes:7-8 even cites the docs file), same memoized members map (notes:98 / docs:71), same non-configurable+non-writable own-property carve-out in get (notes:112-115 / docs:84-87), same batch(fn) run-the-body case (notes:127-136 / docs:104-112), and the identical trap set with near-identical bodies: set/defineProperty/deleteProperty => false, getPrototypeOf => null, setPrototypeOf => false, preventExtensions => false, isExtensible => true, plus the same has / getOwnPropertyDescriptor / ownKeys non-configurable filters (notes:149-190 / docs:122-167). The claimed divergence is real too: READ_ONLY_VIEWS idempotence (notes:43,94,193) and HISTORY_METHODS (notes:35,125-126) exist only in the notes copy. @wafflebase/core exists as the documented shared-logic home (shared-core-extraction.md:117-137) and ships only tokens/geometry/url/image, so nothing was extracted. Duplication/reuse is in this lens's lane, so not out-of-scope, and no guard makes it unreachable. Counter-material exists on severity: shared-core-extraction.md:46-48 lists "Store abstraction unification" as an explicit Non-Goal and :241-243 defers store extraction until a second consumer exists, while notes.md:293-309 and sharing.md:178-183 deliberately document the notes proxy as the "sibling" of the docs one, and HISTORY_METHODS is an interface difference (notes undo/redo return NoteSelection|null; docs' return void) rather than divergent hardening. That makes major-vs-minor arguable, but documenting a copy records the duplication rather than removing it, and ~100 lines of identical security-adjacent proxy machinery that has already diverged is the "duplicated logic that will now diverge" case the rubric treats as blocking. I cannot concretely refute that grading, so the finding stands.
